page: Vultr vx1-m-32c-256g-1920s is an x86_64 cloud server instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores on an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, supporting two threads per core. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory allocation totals 256.0 GB of RAM, offering 8.0 GB per vCPU. The server bundles 1920 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, but does not include GPU accelerators.

Instruction set extensions encompass AVX-512 flags including AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and AVX-512F, along with cryptographic features such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate top-tier uncached memory write bandwidth at 193.78 GB/sec and strong uncached read bandwidth reaching 293.61 GB/sec. The instance delivers a PassMark memory score of 2989.67 alongside a multi-threaded PassMark CPU score of 62405.63. Single-threaded compression performance shows notable throughput, scoring 40.79 GB/sec in gzip compression.

Real-world application tests highlight 63.9 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and 76.18 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based small-model language generation achieves 300.46 tokens per second, though multi-core compilation tasks under Clang fall into average percentiles. Given the high memory-to-core ratio paired with dedicated local NVMe storage, this profile efficiently targets in-memory caching systems, intermediate database operations, ETL data pipelines, and search engine backend workloads.
description: Vultr vx1-m-32c-256g-1920s is an x86_64 instance from the VX1 Cloud Compute line configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores) on an AMD EPYC 2.0 GHz processor, 256.0 GB of RAM, and 1920 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. It lacks GPU acceleration but incorporates broad AVX-512 vector support and robust cryptographic extensions. Benchmark testing indicates high uncached memory bandwidth, with write speeds reaching 193.78 GB/sec, leading to strong throughput in Redis SET operations (63.9 million ops/sec) and database metrics. Its 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio represents a memory-dense hardware design, making it well suited for memory-intensive enterprise tasks such as distributed in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-throughput web serving, and data-intensive batch processing.
